Triage: lands in `scripts/__tests__/spawned-vitest-child-env-8616.test.ts` ⇒ **`domain:devx`**; **type `Bug`, `priority:p3`, `pm:queue`.**

**A false green, which is the class this board grades on its own terms.** The gate derives its population by **AST** — that half is real and its header explains why a substring census would not be one — and then judges each spawn with a **token-presence test over the resolved `env:` text**. ⇒ A spawn passes when that text merely *contains* `childVitestEnv`, **including inside a comment**.

⭐ The card's own scoping is the part to keep: it is a **narrower** hole than objectui#8712, ⛔ not the same defect one gate over. Grading it as a duplicate of #8712 would lose that.

⚠️ ⛔ **Do not weaken the AST half while fixing the judgement half.** The population derivation is the good part; the defect is entirely in what the gate concludes about each member.

`priority:p3`: no leak has been measured through it — objectui#8616 is closed and its gate is not that card's surface. It is a gate that *could* pass something it should refuse, ⛔ not one that has.

## Grading confirmed before dispatch

⭐ Checked that this card's `pm:queue` is triage's and not a filer's, which is a two-second comparison this seat had not been doing: `created_at` 2026-09-10T17:42:54Z vs `updated_at` 18:29:14Z — **46 minutes apart**, one comment from the triage seat, `finding` removed, type `Bug` set. ⇒ a real grading pass. (I skipped objectui#8587 on this fire for the opposite reading: its two timestamps are identical to the second, so every label on it is the filer's.)

## The premise, re-derived on `origin/main` — ⛔ and this one is quoted, not described

`scripts/__tests__/spawned-vitest-child-env-8616.test.ts`, the judgement line, verbatim:

```js
const leaking = SPAWNS.filter((s) => s.env === null || !s.env.includes('childVitestEnv')).map(
```

⇒ ✅ **the defect is exactly where the card says it is.** The population is derived by AST; the per-spawn verdict is `String.prototype.includes` over the resolved `env:` **text**, and a comment sitting inside that declaration's span is part of that text. A spawn passes by **naming** the helper — which is precisely the spelling the sibling gate's own header calls out as the thing to refuse: a call site somebody explained instead of fixing.

⚠️ **One reading that will save you a wrong fix.** There is a *second* `includes` in this file, and it is **not** the defect:

```js
if (!text.includes('vitest')) return [];
```

That one is a cheap pre-filter inside the **population walk** — the half triage explicitly protects. ⛔ Do not touch it, and ⛔ do not "fix" it for symmetry.

## The deliverable

Judge the environment by **what it IS**, not by what its text contains: resolve the `env:` expression and require that it **is** a call to `childVitestEnv` (or spreads one), by AST. objectui#8712's branch does the analogous thing one gate over — the env expression is classified by what it *does* to the key, so a comment about it resolves to nothing.

⭐ **The card handed you the acceptance probe already built**, with its control. Reproduce it before you change anything, then show it inverted:

| probe | expected before | expected after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **control** — the file with a comment that does **not** name the helper | **exit 1**, `1 failed \| 4 passed`, naming the probe's spawn | **exit 1**, unchanged |
| **hole** — the same file whose comment reads `// childVitestEnv() would be the right thing to use here.` | ⛔ **exit 0**, `5 passed` | **exit 1** |

⭐ The control is the load-bearing half and the card says why: it proves the probe really is in this gate's population and really is refused when the helper is absent, so the green in row two is **the predicate accepting it**, ⛔ not the walk failing to see it. Keep that structure — a fix demonstrated without the control is indistinguishable from a fix that broke the walk.

⛔ Remove the probe file after each run **and verify its absence**, as the card's own round did.

## ⛔ Fences — binding

- ⚠️ ⛔ **Do not weaken the AST half while fixing the judgement half** (triage, verbatim). The population derivation is the good part; the defect is entirely in what the gate **concludes** about each member.
- ⛔ **Must not reduce the assertion counts of the four pinned files** objectui#8616 already protects — a floor exists over them. ⛔ Never lower a floor.
- ⚠️ The population walk, the floor, the named member and the live `isAgent` probe in that file are all **sound** and were disputed by no measurement. ⛔ Only the per-spawn membership test is at issue.
- ⛔ **Not a re-litigation of objectui#8616**, and ⛔ not a proposal to weaken the gate.
- ⛔ **Not a duplicate of objectui#8712** — it is a *narrower* hole. There, presence was the wrong test outright, because the goal was **removal**, so a tree that SET the variable passed a gate that existed to remove it. Here presence of the helper **is** the goal, so the only reachable hole is text that names it without calling it. ⭐ Keep that distinction in the PR body; collapsing the two loses the card.
- ⛔ **Worktree-first**; ⛔ **never `git stash`** — `refs/stash` is shared across worktrees and a `pop` takes another agent's entry while reporting **success**.
- ⛔ Governed surface out of scope; ⛔ never edit `content/docs/releases/`; ⛔ never rebase/amend/force-push a pushed branch.
- ⛔ **Cleanup is gated on `git rev-parse HEAD` == `git ls-remote origin <branch>`**, ⛔ never on "the PR is open".

## ⚠️ Concurrency

A sibling `os-dev` is writing prose in `scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` for objectui#7848. ⛔ Do not touch that file.

## Discipline

- ⚠️ **`pnpm lint` in this repo is `turbo run lint` (per-package `eslint .`), ⛔ NOT `eslint . --no-inline-config`.** That flag reports 95 errors and 12,934 warnings on an **untouched** tree by stripping disable directives CI honours; those numbers are ⛔ not a regression. A round today lost time to this.
- ⛔ A grep line count is not an entity count — exclude comment lines (`grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*(\*|//|/\*)'`) and **print the matched lines**. ⭐ On this card that rule is the subject matter, not just the method.
- Every absence claim needs a control with a **known direction that HITS in the same run**; "exactly once" beats "zero" wherever a tombstone should survive.
- Exit codes by **redirect-then-capture**, ⛔ never through a pipe.
- Gates by required context with verdict lines quoted: `Test (shard N/4)`, `Type Check`, `Lint`, `Changeset Declaration`, `Control Byte Scan`.
- ⛔ A ruling is not a reading, a report is not a reading, and the quoted line above is a reading of mine — redo it.

## Deliverable

A worktree, branch `claude/issue-9013-ast-child-vitest-env-membership`, commits, a push, a **draft** PR that `Fixes #9013`.
